subject: Geo stewardship and deletion commitments for hosted API
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@veridianbank.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security@veridianbank.com
Date: 2028-03-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questionnaire: geo stewardship and deletion commitments

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this — Veridian's InfoSec team is compiling vendor answers for our regulatory review. A few specific items we need clarified for the hosted API:  

1) Can you confirm in which cloud regions customer-provided content (API inputs and generated outputs) may be stored at rest and in logs? We need a list of possible locations and whether customers can restrict to a single region.
2) What are your standard retention windows for: (a) request logs, (b) telemetry/metrics, (c) cached KV/prefix data, (d) backups and snapshots?
3) Describe the deletion process when a customer requests a data purge: steps, actors, and expected timelines (including backups/snapshots).
4) If Veridian requires region-bound erasure (all data removed from a region and its backups), what process and timeline can you commit to?

Can you send a brief written response and any supporting artifacts? Please include any SLA exclusions.

Appreciate it — we have a compliance checkpoint 3/16.

Olivia
Olivia Grant
Vendor Risk Lead, Veridian Bank

Attachments: n/a
From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@veridianbank.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-03-09T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questionnaire: geo stewardship and deletion commitments

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers plus two supporting artifacts (SOC2 summary and a regional data flow diagram). I'll keep this high level; happy to jump on a short call if you want implementation details.

1) Storage locations and region restrictions
- Hosted API: customer inputs and generated outputs are processed in the region of the serving cluster chosen by routing policy. By default, requests are routed to nearest available region (US, EU, APAC).
- Persistent logs (audit and request metadata) and longer-term telemetry may be replicated to a central analytics cluster for billing and platform health (US primary).
- Customer-level regional restriction: customers on our Dedicated or Private offerings can enforce single-region residency. For hosted API, customers can request a regional pin for their tenant (contract addendum). Regional pinning is supported operationally but requires a short provisioning window (see timelines).

2) Standard retention windows (default hosted API)
- Request logs (metadata): 30 days by default; can be shortened via support request for customers with contract-level privacy needs.
- Full request payloads (inputs/outputs): by default ephemeral; retained for 7 days for debugging and quality safeguards unless otherwise agreed.
- Telemetry and aggregated metrics: 365 days for platform health and billing analytics (aggregated/anonymized by default).
- Cache / KV (prefix + model cache): eviction is workload-driven; KV entries are ephemeral and typically expire within 24–72 hours, with explicit prefix cache invalidation available via API.
- Backups & snapshots: persisted snapshots of model-serving state and storage backups are retained up to 90 days (rolling), with incremental snapshots retained per our backup schedule.

3) Deletion process and timelines
- Customer erasure request: 1) request submitted via support portal or signed request, 2) verification by account owner, 3) enqueue purge job on tenant, 4) purge job removes tenant data from live storage and clears caches, 5) record deletion event in audit log.
- Expected timelines: live data and caches cleared within 72 hours after verification; removal from most backups completed within 30–90 days depending on snapshot retention and backup retention window.
- Actors: Customer (request), Support (verify), Platform Ops (supervise purge), Automation (execute purge jobs).
- Evidence: We provide an erasure report and audit log entry when the job completes.

4) Region-bound erasure commitment (contracted)
- For a firm requirement to remove all customer data from a specific region and associated backups, we offer a contractual addendum. Process: identify tenant instances in-region, initiate purge job and regional metadata sweep, rotate encryption keys for that tenant to cryptographically orphan residual encrypted backups where immediate physical deletion from region is not feasible, regenerate evidence and submit attestation.
- Timeline commitment (with addendum): 30 business days to complete region-bound erasure and provide attestation; emergency/accelerated options can be negotiated for an additional fee.

SLA exclusions and notes
- Third-party cloud provider redundancy and immutable long-term logs (customer-provided replication outside our control) may affect timelines.
- Cryptographic orphaning is used where immediate removal from off-site immutable backups is technically infeasible; this meets many regulatory requirements but should be reviewed by legal for your jurisdiction.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf), geo-data-flow-diagram.png (image)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@veridianbank.com>

Subject: Re: Questionnaire: geo stewardship and deletion commitments

Kimberly — thanks, this is helpful. Two quick clarifications:  

A) You say full payloads are "ephemeral" and retained for 7 days by default. Can you confirm whether customers can opt-out of payload retention entirely (zero days) on hosted API without moving to Dedicated/Private?

B) On backups: for the 30–90 day removal window, can you clarify whether you perform any proactive snapshot scrubbing for a tenant once an erasure is requested (i.e., do you attempt to remove older incrementals beyond cryptographic rotation)?

Olivia
From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@veridianbank.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-03-10T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questionnaire: geo stewardship and deletion commitments

Hi Olivia — quick follow-up answers:  

A) Opt-out for payload retention on hosted API
Short answer: Yes, with caveats. We can disable ephemeral payload retention for a hosted-API tenant via a configuration flag that prevents routing of payloads to persistent debug logs. This setting is available without moving to Dedicated/Private but requires a signed configuration request and may disable certain platform debugging features (e.g., prioritized support for reproducing errors). We log the configuration change in the account audit trail.

B) Snapshot handling after erasure request
- Default behavior: we do not retroactively rewrite historical incremental snapshots across provider-managed immutable snapshot layers because those systems often lack in-place rewrite capability.
- Proactive scrubbing: for customers with a contractual region-bound erasure addendum we will attempt targeted scrub operations where provider APIs permit it; where not possible we will perform cryptographic key rotation to orphan data and provide attestation.
- Timeline: scrub attempts will be started immediately after verification and completed within the contractual 30 business day window when an addendum is in place.

Neha (cc'd) — I tagged you because sales may want to attach the regional pin addendum language to Veridian's quote. Ben — FYI in case Veridian requests evidence or escalation.

Best,
Kimberly
